snippet.title: Why MrBeast is Actually Broke
snippet.description:
Welcome to Money's Hidden Past! Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, has an estimated net worth of $2.6 billion in 2026. Yet, the biggest creator on Earth famously claims to have a bank account in the red. How is that mathematically possible?

The answer lies in the ultimate compounding business model. MrBeast doesn't just make videos; he runs Beast Industries, a massive media and consumer goods conglomerate. From generating hundreds of millions through Feastables chocolate to securing massive streaming deals, his revenue streams are vast. But instead of taking a massive personal payout, he aggressively reinvests nearly every single dollar back into the company to fund even bigger spectacles. Join us as we break down the financial architecture of the MrBeast empire, and reveal why the smartest way to build a multi-billion-dollar valuation is to stay completely "broke" on paper.

Subscribe for Money's Hidden Past deep dives into the real mechanics of wealth and business empires. Comment below: Is MrBeast's strategy of endless reinvestment genius, or too risky?

snippet.title: Italian Michelin-Star Chef Rates 21 Italian Food Scenes From Movies And TV | Insider
snippet.description:
Chef and restaurateur Cesare Casella breaks down Italian cuisine scenes from movies and TV based on realism.

Casella discusses the accuracy of the meatballs from "The Godfather," pasta sauce and thin garlic in "Goodfellas," and capicola in "The Sopranos." He also analyzes a dish from "Lady and the Tramp" (1955), timpano from "Big Night," the tiramisu in "Superbad," and carbonara from "Master of None." He breaks down the pasta twirling technique from "Brooklyn," cannoli from "The Bear," and calzone from "Parks and Rec." Casella reviews proper pizza throwing technique from "Seinfeld," pizza-eating form in "Eat Pray Love," lasagna-making in "Garfield: A Tale of Two Kitties," mozzarella sandwiches from "Bicycle Thieves," take-out salads from "Family Guy," Italian kitchen-table dining in "Amarcord," and trenette al pesto from "Luca."

Casella has been cooking for more than 50 years and served as the head chef at the Michelin-starred restaurant Vipore in Italy. He then moved to the United States and worked at several fine-dining Italian restaurants in New York City such as Beppe and Salumeria Rosi. Today, Casella is head of the Department of Nourishment Arts at the Center for Discovery, a residential facility in upstate New York for the medically fragile. He oversees a team of chefs, nutritionists, therapists, farmers, and educators.

snippet.title: Surviving Earth's Most Extreme Climates (Full Episode) | Hostile Planet: Compilation | Nat Geo
snippet.description:
Hosted by Bear Grylls, Hostile Planet zooms in on the world’s most extreme environments to reveal the animal kingdom’s epic stories of survival on this fast-changing and continuously evolving planet. In this Hostile Planet compilation from National Geographic, discover the animals that call deserts and the Earth’s poles home. 

Surviving the Desert - 0:00
How do animals survive in the desert? Desert wildlife relies on specialized adaptations to combat extreme heat, dehydration, and a lack of shade where the sun is the ultimate enemy. For desert animals like the Nubian ibex, Arabian wolf, and brown hyena, to survive in the desert means learning how to deal with the sun’s unrelenting volatility. 

Polar Habitats - 0:47:07
Polar habitats are similarly enslaved by the sun: half the year is plunged into bitterly cold darkness and hardship, and the other half is blistered with light and heat. What animals live in polar habitats? Polar regions are home to highly resilient species like polar bears, Arctic wolves, emperor penguins, musk ox, and more that are uniquely built to survive months of freezing darkness and sudden seasonal shifts. As the sun exerts its unquestionable dominance, we reveal the incredible ways these wild animals survive.
